newsitem.title: CANADA: Snow may force some North Alberta crop switching.
newsitem.headline: Snow may force some North Alberta crop switching.

text.p: Weekend rain followed by snow on Wednesday in Alberta's Peace River Valley may force some crop switching as the likely number of frost-free growing days shrink to near 100 in the area, an Alberta crop expert said.

"There is the potential that some acres will switch from spring wheat, peas and Argentine canola into (lower yielding, faster maturing) Polish canola, oats and barley," Wendy Boje, Alberta Agriculture crop statistician, told Reuters.

"In Grande Prairie (southern Peace River Valley) they've got 50 to 60 percent of the crop in. Any crop that was put in the Peace last week would have been spring wheat, peas ... so it's not going to be a huge movement and they plant a lot of feed grains up there," Boje said.
The Canadian Wheat Board said 75 percent of intended acreage had been seeded across Alberta by Tuesday.
But northern areas were hit by weekend rains and 20 cm (8 inches) of snow Wednesday which may delay seeding to May 24, Boje said.
Killing frosts could strike Alberta's Peace River Valley by the end of August, 102 days from Wednesday, Boje said.

Wheat needs 90 to 100 days to mature, barley 60 to 90 days, oats 85 to 88 days and flax 85 to 100 days. Also, Argentine canola needs 92 to 102 days, Polish canola 73 to 83 days and field peas 90 to 100 days, specialists have said.
There are 100 days from May 23 to August 31.
Grande Prairie's earliest frost was recorded August 15 and in Calgary August 16, Alberta Agriculture statistics show.

Statistics Canada on April 30 forecast Alberta spring wheat seeded acreage for this spring at 6.0 million acres, canola at 3.8 million acres, oats at 1.45 million acres, barley at 5.65 million acres and peas at 450,000 acres.
Planting was 80 percent complete in the south and center.
"At this time, it would appear that producers in the southern and central regions will maintain the intentions they made earlier," Boje said.
